Question: What is the difference between Data Analytics, Data Analysis, Data Mining, Data Science, Machine Learning, and Big Data?
Answer: Data Analytics: This refers to the process of inspecting, transforming and modeling data to discover useful information, suggest conclusions and support decision making. Analytics uses techniques from statistics, machine learning, and visualization. It is a broad field that encompasses multiple types of analysis. Data Analysis: This refers to examining raw data to obtain useful information and derive conclusions. It involves using analytical tools and techniques to organize and interrogate data with the goal of summarizing it into useful insights. Data analysis is a subset of data analytics focused more on deriving insights from historical data. Data Mining: This involves searching large amounts of data for patterns and relationships that can be considered useful. It uses statistical, machine learning and artificial intelligence techniques to discover patterns in large datasets that can help predict future behavior and trends. Data mining can be seen as a more advanced form of data analysis focused on automated discovery of insights. Data Science: This encompasses the broad set of skills, techniques and approaches needed to extract insights from data. It includes data analytics, machine learning, statistical modeling and data visualization. Data scientists combine expertise in mathematics, programming and domain knowledge to analyze complex datasets and build data-driven solutions. Machine Learning: This is a subset of artificial intelligence that uses statistical techniques to give computers the ability to "learn" from data without being explicitly programmed. Machine learning algorithms "learn" by analyzing training data to identify patterns, make predictions or perform tasks. When given new data, they can apply what they've "learned" to yield useful results. Big Data: This refers to the enormous volumes of data that businesses now have available due to the digital world we live in. Big data has three main characteristics: volume, velocity and variety. Industry analysts say any dataset exceeding terabytes or petabytes in size qualifies as "big data." Big data technologies and techniques enable the extraction of value from these massive datasets. Question: What do you know that most people don’t?
Answer: If you notice the refill of a gel pen minutely you would notice that it has two separate ink fluids. The gel ink of the pen, and a transparent fluid at the end that is called the stopper fluid. Composition of Gel Pen Ink Gel pen ink is a type of water-based ink that is thickened with a gelling agent. This gelling agent is usually a polymer that is suspended in water and forms a three-dimensional network of molecules. The thickness of the gel ink is what gives it its unique texture and consistency when compared to other types of ink. The pigments used in gel ink are also different than those used in other types of ink. Gel ink pigments are usually smaller and more finely ground, which allows for a more even and consistent color distribution. This is why gel ink is often used for coloring and drawing, as it can produce brighter and more vivid colors than other types of ink. Stopper Fluid: The Unsung Hero of Gel Pens One of the key components of a gel pen is the stopper fluid. This is a viscous liquid that is added to the ink to help regulate its flow. Without stopper fluid, gel ink would flow too freely and could cause the pen to leak or smudge. Stopper fluid is typically made from silicone oil or a similar substance that has a high viscosity. Whenthe pen is not in use, the stopper fluid helps to keep the ink in place and prevent it from drying out. When the pen is in use, the stopper fluid helps to control the flow of ink and ensure that it is smooth and consistent. Stopper fluid is like the unsung hero of gel pens. It's always there, doing its job to regulate ink flow and prevent smudging, but we hardly ever notice it. It's like the Robin to Batman, always in the background but crucial to the success of the mission. So next time you're using a gel pen, take a moment to appreciate the stopper fluid and all the hard work it does to make your writing or drawing experience smooth and enjoyable. Signing off, LOKI

Question: What is the difference between GDP and GNP?
Answer: GDP and GNP are two key measurements of a country's economic output. Understanding the difference between the two can help clarify how a country’s economy is evaluated. Gross domestic product, or GDP, refers to the total value of goods and services produced within a country's borders during a specific time period. It aims to measure everything produced domestically. Gross national product, or GNP, is slightly different. GNP includes GDP but also adds the net income a country's citizens and businesses earn abroad. So in simple terms: GDP = Value of goods and services produced within a country's borders GNP = GDP + Net income earned abroad Let me break this down further: GDP focuses only on production within a country's physical borders. It looks at output created by domestic residents and organizations, regardless of where the income is actually earned. For example, if a US company makes $100 million by selling products to customers in India, that $100 million would be included in the US GDP. This is because the production happened within the US, even though the income was earned here in India. In contrast, GNP factors in income earned abroad by residents of that country. So in the example I gave above, GNP would include that same $100 million in output but would then subtract any production costs and foreign taxes paid. The net income earned abroad is added to GDP to calculate GNP. Therefore, GNP reflects the total income of a country's citizens from all sources, both domestic and foreign. It provides a more accurate and realistic picture of the resources available for domestic consumption. Signing off, LOKI

While the Tupolev-144 was Russian made, the Concorde was made possible by a joint Anglo-French effort. But despite their impressive speed and luxurious amenities, these planes were ultimately grounded for several reasons. High operating costs Noise Pollution Safety concerns Environmental impact FUTURE OF SUPERSONIC TRAVEL So, given all these concerns, is there any hope for supersonic travel in the future? So, while the Concorde and Tupolev 144 may be a thing of the past, the future of supersonic travel looks promising. Question: What are a few bitter truths of life?
Answer: None really. Why shall a truth be bitter in the first place? People often compare a truth to a burning torchlight of justice. The next moment, I find them calling it a nessecary “evil”. And eventually, as we move through the alleys of our lives this same truth becomes bitter. The whole aroma of truth, mostly revolves around how it pricks into our souls. Sometimes, truths bring the warmest smiles and happiest tears to our eyes. Like a melody written in the pages of our heart, we embrace it with open arms, shower marigolds and daisies on it. And maybe that is how many promises of lifetime are made. For they are truths, truths of the moment, for sure. For truths that make the crystal clear waters of our heart unclear, we usually tend to be dissmissive of them. Those same truths, once showered of love, are now veiled into beautifully crafted lies. Why, have they lost their appeal? So you decorate your heart with lies, which you know will only make it worse. Then, arrives the day when truth becomes bitter. Like the stale food in the kitchen, which you have craved for before, but now it is unconsumable. You can neither enjoy its taste, nor throw it away. They say truth flows of bitterness, but so sweet it is; still, the pages written of truth is where lies beauty. It pains me— to see my face, distorted of the lies I made. They say truth brings hate and war, but it is adored on my doorstep; the smell of truth fills my heart. It pains me— to see your eyes, burning of rage, among my heart. One of the bitterest truths of life, is that, truth is never bitter itself. We often forget to embrace it. It rots among the decorated lies we gift our heart. And then one day, it is stale, bitter, unconsumable. Signing off, LOKI

Question: Why do we sometimes become sad for no reason?
Answer: Sad for no reason you say. Sometimes, wandering among the burial grounds, a similar thought came to me aswell. To be sad, does it need a reason? I walked, from one tombstone to another, reading the names on the plaques. We can be sad. Does it really have to be clear enough to have a reason. If there had been a single definite reason for our sadness, to embed happy and cherished imprints over them would be so easy. But it never is, rather our sadness often becomes chronic. There are strings, always, a intricate web which wraps around you. The web, wont let us fall to the ground, to stand up again. Neither will it let us go of its grasp. The stench of sadness breeds among the web that binds us to the imprints of our sorrows. Sometimes, these sorrows are long gone, clouded visions in your subconcious. That often makes us feel sad with no apparent reason in sight. Signing off, LOKI
